patch.value: Point-in-time reconstruction gate: prove every item at every recorded version replays exactly from its history stream alone

The restorability promise is that any item can be returned to any version at any time, and point-in-time reads already exist. What is not proven is the general case: that for every item in a workspace, and every version in its stream, replaying the stream from the beginning reproduces exactly the state that read returns, using nothing but the immutable history. Today's coverage tests the mechanism on chosen cases; the promise is universal and therefore needs a universal check. Make it a gate: for a workspace corpus that includes real-shaped history — items that were renamed, retyped, reparented, redacted, compacted, restored, merged from divergent branches, and closed and reopened — replay every version of every item from its stream and assert byte-identical agreement with the point-in-time projection, with the item file itself used only as an independent third comparison and never as the source. Disagreement is a data-integrity defect by definition. Compaction and redaction are the interesting cases and must be covered explicitly, since both rewrite what a replay can see and must preserve reconstructability of every version they claim to retain.

For every item and every recorded version in the test corpus, replay from the history stream alone reproduces the point-in-time projection exactly; The current item file is used only as an independent third comparison, never as an input to the replay, asserted by the test's construction; The corpus includes items that were renamed, retyped, reparented, redacted, compacted, restored, merged from divergent branches, and closed and reopened; Compacted streams are covered explicitly: every version the compaction claims to retain still replays exactly, and versions it dropped are reported as intentionally unavailable rather than silently wrong; Redacted streams replay to a state that omits the redacted content while keeping every other field and the chain verifiable; A mismatch fails the gate with the item, version, and diverging field named, so the failure is diagnosable without rerunning by hand
The restorability promise is a checked property of every item and every version, not a demonstrated capability of the restore command
Restorability and provable history are the durability promise; a promise that holds for the cases someone remembered to test is not a promise
Adds an exhaustive replay check over a history corpus; expected to surface reconstruction gaps around compaction, redaction, and merge-union streams
Any recorded state of any item is provably reachable from immutable history alone

message: File the universal reconstruction gate that the restorability promise requires
